chunks: My father (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, from al-Ya'qubi, from Isa ibn Abdullah al-Alawi, from his father, from Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali al-Baqir, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them). He said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and his family) said:

Whoever would be pleased to traverse the Path like a strong wind and enter Paradise without reckoning, then let him accept the guardianship of my friend, my deputy, my companion, and my vicegerent over my family and my nation -- Ali ibn Abi Talib. And whoever would be pleased to enter the Fire, then let him abandon his guardianship.

For by my Lord's majesty and glory, he is indeed the gate of Allah that cannot be approached except through him, and he is the Straight Path, and he is the one about whose guardianship Allah will ask on the Day of Resurrection.

key_terms.الصراط: The Sirat -- a bridge over Hell that all must cross on the Day of Judgment; speed of crossing reflects one's faith
key_terms.خليفة: Khalifa -- vicegerent, one appointed to lead the community after the Prophet
key_terms.وصي: Wasi -- designated successor/executor of the Prophet's spiritual and temporal authority
key_terms.ولاية: Wilaya -- guardianship, authority, and spiritual allegiance to Ali and the Imams

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about Ali ibn Abi Talib being the gate of Allah and the Straight Path?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) declares the supreme station of Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), calling him his friend, deputy, companion, and vicegerent. He states that accepting Ali's wilaya (authority/guardianship) is the means of swiftly crossing the Sirat on the Day of Judgment and entering Paradise without reckoning. The Prophet also identifies Ali as 'the gate of Allah' and 'the Straight Path' -- the one about whose authority all will be questioned on the Day of Resurrection. This hadith was delivered to the Muslim community as a declaration of Ali's unique role in the divinely appointed chain of authority after the Prophet.
